Load, clean, combine data [hidden in output]

TOPX

# load in data
dat_topx <- read.csv("data/aggregate_topx_20260414.csv")

# set the levels for variable "visit"
dat_topx$visit <- factor(dat_topx$visit,
                         levels = c("BL1", "BL2", "6M", "7M", "12M"))

# how many ppts total? (n = 201)
length(unique(dat_topx$subj))
## [1] 201
dat_topx <- dat_topx %>%
  rename(group = subj_type) %>%
  mutate(
    group_num = case_when(
      group == "Control" ~ 0,
      group == "Patient" ~ 1))

# keep only ppts with BL1, BL2, and 6M (n = 105)
proj3_visits <- c("BL1", "BL2", "6M")
dat_topx_proj3 <- dat_topx %>% 
  group_by(subj) %>% 
  filter(all(proj3_visits %in% visit)) %>% 
  ungroup()
length(unique(dat_topx_proj3$subj))
## [1] 105
# remove BL2
dat_topx_proj3 <- dat_topx_proj3 %>% 
  filter(visit %in% c("BL1", "6M"))
# set this to dataframe going forward, if using for analyses
dat_topx <- dat_topx_proj3

# keep only ppts with all visits, BL1 through 12M (n = 32)
proj4_visits <- c("BL1", "BL2", "6M", "7M", "12M")
dat_topx_proj4 <- dat_topx %>% 
  group_by(subj) %>% 
  filter(all(proj4_visits %in% visit)) %>% 
  ungroup()
length(unique(dat_topx_proj4$subj))
## [1] 0

Demographics

Clinical Symptoms

BPRS

# read in bprs data
dat_bprs <- read.csv("data/step_bprs_clean_20260417.csv")

#rename variables 
colnames(dat_bprs)[1] <- "subj"
dat_bprs <- dat_bprs %>%
  rename(bprs_pos_ws = bprs_pos_ws_avg,
         bprs_neg_ws = bprs_neg_ws_avg,
         bprs_disorg_ws = bprs_disorg_ws_avg,
         bprs_mania_ws = bprs_mania_ws_avg,
         bprs_dep_anx_ws = bprs_dep_anx_ws_avg)

# add variable for group
dat_bprs$group = "group"
dat_bprs <- dat_bprs %>% 
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      str_sub(subj, 1, 3) == 'SP1' ~ 'Control',
      str_sub(subj, 1, 3) == 'SP2' ~ 'Patient',
      TRUE ~ group)) %>% 
  mutate(
    group_num = case_when(
      group == "Control" ~ 0,
      group == "Patient" ~ 1))

# subset bprs data by topx data
dat_bprs <- dat_bprs %>%
  filter(subj %in% dat_topx$subj)

GROUP DIFF

Demographics

Gender

# gender - using fisher because samples are too small for chi-squared
fisher.test(dat_demo$gender, dat_demo$group)
## 
##  Fisher's Exact Test for Count Data
## 
## data:  dat_demo$gender and dat_demo$group
## p-value = 0.01809
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided

Age

# age
# welch's two-sample t-test
t.test(age ~ group_num, data = dat_demo)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  age by group_num
## t = 0.30219, df = 98.594, p-value = 0.7631
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group 0 and group 1 is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -1.903975  2.588071
## sample estimates:
## mean in group 0 mean in group 1 
##        26.18519        25.84314
# test variance/normality to see if t-tests are appropriate
leveneTest(dat_demo$age, dat_demo$group_num, data = dat_demo) # tests equal variance between groups
## Warning in leveneTest.default(dat_demo$age, dat_demo$group_num, data =
## dat_demo): dat_demo$group_num coerced to factor.
## Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = median: dat_demo)
##        Df F value Pr(>F)
## group   1  1.6227 0.2056
##       103
shapiro.test(dat_demo$age) # tests normality
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  dat_demo$age
## W = 0.93629, p-value = 7.731e-05
# wilcox aka mann-whitney U test
wilcox.test(age ~ group_num, data = dat_demo)
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  age by group_num
## W = 1308.5, p-value = 0.6622
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

Race

# race - using fisher because samples are too small for chi-squared

##

##

LONGITUDINAL

TOPX

Error

# run the LMER, report as an ANOVA
mod_err <- lmer(error ~ group * trial_type * visit + (1|subj), data = dat_topx)
anova_err <- anova(mod_err, type = 3)
anova_err
## Type III Analysis of Variance Table with Satterthwaite's method
##                        Sum Sq Mean Sq NumDF  DenDF F value    Pr(>F)    
## group                  0.1143 0.11433     1 103.03  4.8418  0.030011 *  
## trial_type             5.9624 1.98748     3 725.05 84.1680 < 2.2e-16 ***
## visit                  0.0050 0.00503     1 725.35  0.2131  0.644511    
## group:trial_type       0.4366 0.14553     3 725.05  6.1629  0.000387 ***
## group:visit            0.0011 0.00107     1 725.35  0.0452  0.831662    
## trial_type:visit       0.0291 0.00970     3 725.05  0.4109  0.745202    
## group:trial_type:visit 0.0081 0.00272     3 725.05  0.1150  0.951324    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# run post-hoc tests on LMER main and significant effects
print(emmeans(mod_err, list(pairwise ~ group), adjust = "mvt"))
## NOTE: Results may be misleading due to involvement in interactions
## $`emmeans of group`
##  group   emmean     SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
##  Control  0.133 0.0178 103   0.0972    0.168
##  Patient  0.189 0.0183 103   0.1524    0.225
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: trial_type, visit 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## 
## $`pairwise differences of group`
##  1                 estimate     SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  Control - Patient  -0.0562 0.0255 103  -2.200  0.0300
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: trial_type, visit 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger
print(emmeans(mod_err, list(pairwise ~ trial_type), adjust = "mvt"))
## NOTE: Results may be misleading due to involvement in interactions
## $`emmeans of trial_type`

Error Aff/NonAff

dat_topx <- dat_topx %>%
  left_join(
    dat_demo %>% select(subj, dx_affect),
    by = "subj"
  )

dat_topx <- dat_topx %>%
  mutate(dx_affect = ifelse(group == "Control" & is.na(dx_affect),
                            1,
                            dx_affect))

dat_topx$dx_affect <- factor(dat_topx$dx_affect,
                             levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                             labels = c("Ctl", "Non-Aff", "Aff"))


# run the LMER, report as an ANOVA
mod_err_aff <- lmer(error ~ dx_affect * trial_type * visit + (1|subj), data = dat_topx)
anova_err_aff <- anova(mod_err_aff, type = 3)
anova_err_aff
## Type III Analysis of Variance Table with Satterthwaite's method
##                            Sum Sq Mean Sq NumDF  DenDF F value    Pr(>F)    
## dx_affect                  0.2666 0.13328     2 101.90  5.7079  0.004471 ** 
## trial_type                 5.4439 1.81464     3 717.97 77.7149 < 2.2e-16 ***
## visit                      0.0052 0.00524     1 718.44  0.2243  0.635914    
## dx_affect:trial_type       0.7299 0.12164     6 717.97  5.2096 2.916e-05 ***
## dx_affect:visit            0.0551 0.02757     2 718.41  1.1809  0.307610    
## trial_type:visit           0.0199 0.00662     3 717.97  0.2835  0.837355    
## dx_affect:trial_type:visit 0.0153 0.00255     6 717.97  0.1094  0.995357    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# run post-hoc tests on LMER main and significant effects
print(emmeans(mod_err_aff, list(pairwise ~ dx_affect), adjust = "mvt"))

Plot All BPRS

Prep data for plot

# add aff/non-aff dx variable to BPRS
dat_bprs <- dat_bprs %>%
  left_join(
    dat_demo %>% select(subj, dx_affect),
    by = "subj"
  )

dat_bprs$dx_affect <- factor(dat_bprs$dx_affect,
                             levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                             labels = c("Ctl", "Non-Aff", "Aff"))

# convert BPRS from wide to long format
dat_bprs_long <- dat_bprs %>% 
  # filter data to only keep variables of interest
  select(c(subj, visit, group, group_num, dx_affect, bprs_pos_ws, bprs_neg_ws,
           bprs_disorg_ws, bprs_mania_ws, bprs_dep_anx_ws)) %>% 
  # convert data to long format
  pivot_longer(cols = c(bprs_pos_ws, bprs_neg_ws, bprs_disorg_ws, 
                        bprs_mania_ws, bprs_dep_anx_ws), 
               names_to = "bprs_symptom", 
               values_to = "bprs_score") %>% 
  # create labels
  mutate(bprs_symptom = dplyr::recode(bprs_symptom,
         "bprs_pos_ws" = "Pos",
         "bprs_neg_ws" = "Neg",
         "bprs_disorg_ws" = "Disorg",
         "bprs_mania_ws" = "Mania",
         "bprs_dep_anx_ws" = "Dep-Anx"),
          # set labels to factors, to appear in specified order
         bprs_symptom = factor(bprs_symptom,
                               levels = c("Pos", "Neg", "Disorg", 
                                          "Mania", "Dep-Anx"))) %>% 
  mutate(group_visit = factor(paste(group, visit, sep = "_"),
                              levels = c("Control_BL1", "Control_6M", 
                                         "Patient_BL1", "Patient_6M"))) %>% 
  mutate(visit = factor(visit,
                        levels = c("BL1", "6M")))

Line plot

# Line plot of BPRS all symptoms
plot_bprs <- ggplot(dat_bprs_long, 
                    aes(x= bprs_symptom, y=bprs_score, 
                            group = interaction(group,visit))) +
  stat_summary(fun="mean", geom="line",
               aes(color = group, linetype = visit),
               linewidth = 1, position = position_dodge(0.2)) +
  stat_summary(fun="mean", geom="point", aes(color = group), 
               size = 2, position = position_dodge(0.2)) + 
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "errorbar", aes(color = group), 
               width = 0.7, size = 1, position = position_dodge(0.2)) + 
  labs(title = "BPRS Symptoms", 
       y = "Average Item Score", 
       x = "Symptom Subfactors", 
       color = "Group", linetype = "Visit") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, NA)) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("#2C737F", "#AA8829"),
                     labels=c("Ctl", "EP")) + 
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed"), 
                        labels = c("Visit 1", "6-Month")) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), 
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"), 
        axis.text = element_text(face="bold", size = 12),

    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    color = "black",
    pattern_fill = "black",
    pattern_color = "black",
    pattern_density = 0.1,
    pattern_spacing = 0.02
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = mean_se,
    geom = "errorbar",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    width = 0.3
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = "BPRS Symptoms",
    y = "Average Item Score",
    x = "Symptom Subfactors", 
    fill = "Group",
    pattern = "Visit"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Control" = "#2C737F", "Patient" = "#AA8829"),
    labels = c("Ctl", "EP")
  ) +
  scale_pattern_manual(
    values = c("BL" = "none", "6M" = "stripe"),
    labels = c("Visit 1", "6-Month")
  ) +
  guides(
  fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(pattern = "none")),
  pattern = guide_legend()
) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),

    legend.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 22)
  )

BPRS (Aff/NonAff)

Total

# run the LMER, report as an ANOVA
mod_bprs2 <- lmer(bprs_total ~ dx_affect * visit + (1|subj), data = dat_bprs)
anova_bprs2 <- anova(mod_bprs2, type = 3)
anova_bprs2
## Type III Analysis of Variance Table with Satterthwaite's method
##                 Sum Sq Mean Sq NumDF  DenDF F value Pr(>F)    
## dx_affect       4210.1 2105.03     2 103.23 69.4999 <2e-16 ***
## visit             60.1   60.10     1 102.05  1.9842 0.1620    
## dx_affect:visit  136.5   68.25     2 101.90  2.2532 0.1103    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# run post-hoc tests on significant effects
print(emmeans(mod_bprs2, list(pairwise ~ dx_affect), adjust = "mvt"))
## NOTE: Results may be misleading due to involvement in interactions
## $`emmeans of dx_affect`
##  dx_affect emmean    SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
##  Ctl         27.8 0.829 101     26.2     29.5
##  Non-Aff     43.5 1.200 102     41.1     45.9
##  Aff         39.7 1.230 104     37.2     42.1
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: visit 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## 
## $`pairwise differences of dx_affect`
##  1               estimate   SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  Ctl - (Non-Aff)   -15.71 1.46 102 -10.756 <0.0001
##  Ctl - Aff         -11.87 1.49 103  -7.984 <0.0001
##  (Non-Aff) - Aff     3.84 1.72 103   2.226  0.0708
## 
## Results are averaged over the levels of: visit 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## P value adjustment: mvt method for 3 tests

# reshape data for plot
dat_gf_long <- dat_gf %>%
  select(subj, visit, group, gfs, gfr) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(gfs, gfr),
    names_to = "gf_type",
    values_to = "gf_score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    gf_type = dplyr::recode(gf_type,
      "gfs" = "GFS",
      "gfr" = "GFR"
    ),
    gf_type = factor(gf_type, levels = c("GFS", "GFR")),
    visit = factor(visit, levels = c("BL1", "6M")),
    group_visit = factor(
      paste(group, visit, sep = "_"),
      levels = c("Control_BL1", "Control_6M", "Patient_BL1", "Patient_6M")
    ))

# plot it
plot_gf_bar <- ggplot(
  dat_gf_long,
  aes(x = gf_type, y = gf_score, fill = group_visit)
) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = "mean",
    geom = "bar",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    color = "black"
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = mean_se,
    geom = "errorbar",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    width = 0.3
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Global Functioning",

      "Control_BL1" = "#2C737F",

    ),
    labels = c("Ctl Visit 1", "Ctl 6-Month", "EP Visit 1", "EP 6-Month")
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),

# create new bprs dataframe with only necessary variables
dat_bprs_abbrev <- dat_bprs %>% 
  select(subj, visit, bprs_total, bprs_pos_ws, bprs_neg_ws, bprs_disorg_ws, bprs_mania_ws, bprs_dep_anx_ws)

# create new topx dataframe, eliminating BL2
dat_topx_abbrev <- dat_topx %>% 
  filter(visit == "BL1" | visit == "6M") 
dat_topx_abbrev <- dat_topx_abbrev %>% 
  select(subj, visit, group, d_context, d_expect, trial_type, rt_mdn, error)
dat_topx_abbrev$visit <- as.character(dplyr::recode(dat_topx_abbrev$visit, "BL1" = "BL"))
dat_topx_abbrev <- pivot_wider(dat_topx_abbrev, 
                               id_cols = c(subj, visit, group, 
                                           d_context, d_expect), 
                               values_from = c(rt_mdn, error), 
                               names_from = trial_type)

# combine topx & bprs data
dat_topx_bprs <- dat_topx_abbrev %>%
  left_join(dat_bprs_abbrev %>% 
              select(subj, visit, bprs_total, bprs_pos_ws, 
                     bprs_neg_ws, bprs_disorg_ws, bprs_mania_ws, 
                     bprs_dep_anx_ws),
    by = c("subj", "visit"))

# create dataframes for each visit
dat_topx_bprs_bl <- dat_topx_bprs %>% 
  filter(visit == "BL")
dat_topx_bprs_6m <- dat_topx_bprs %>% 
  filter(visit == "6M")

Test Normality

# Test normal distribution of variables
# if p < .05, variable is non-normal/skewed 
shapiro.test(dat_topx_bprs$error_AX)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  dat_topx_bprs$error_AX
## W = 0.82952, p-value = 1.816e-14
shapiro.test(dat_topx_bprs$error_AY)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  dat_topx_bprs$error_AY
## W = 0.91015, p-value = 5.446e-10
shapiro.test(dat_topx_bprs$error_BX)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  dat_topx_bprs$error_BX
## W = 0.71636, p-value < 2.2e-16
shapiro.test(dat_topx_bprs$error_BY)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  dat_topx_bprs$error_BY
## W = 0.63334, p-value < 2.2e-16
shapiro.test(dat_topx_bprs$bprs_pos_ws)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  dat_topx_bprs$bprs_pos_ws
## W = 0.56607, p-value = 4.113e-16
shapiro.test(dat_topx_bprs$bprs_neg_ws)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  dat_topx_bprs$bprs_neg_ws
## W = 0.7348, p-value = 1.756e-12
shapiro.test(dat_topx_bprs$bprs_disorg_ws)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  dat_topx_bprs$bprs_disorg_ws
## W = 0.8545, p-value = 9.531e-09

Run correlation

# create dataframe for a correlation matrix of TOPX error rates and BPRS symptoms
dat_cor1 <- dat_topx_bprs %>% 
  select(error_AX, error_AY, error_BX, bprs_pos_ws, bprs_neg_ws, bprs_disorg_ws)

# compute and print correlations + p-values
cor1_results <- rcorr(as.matrix(dat_cor1), type = "spearman")
(cor1_matrix <- cor1_results$r)
##                   error_AX    error_AY   error_BX bprs_pos_ws bprs_neg_ws

## error_AY        0.66835768 1.000000000 0.49383027   0.1261611  0.04456721

## bprs_pos_ws     0.10422052 0.126161060 0.21973839   1.0000000  0.28794472

## bprs_pos_ws       0.612454384
## bprs_neg_ws       0.285900677
## bprs_disorg_ws    1.000000000
(p1_matrix   <- cor1_results$P)

Plot corr matrix

# Plot Spearman correlation matrix with significance masking
filename <- paste0("graphs/", format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d"), "_TOPX_BPRS.png")
col_pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#2C737F", "white", "#A30021"))(100)
colnames(cor1_matrix) <- c("AX Error", "AY Error", "BX Error",
                           "BPRS Positive", "BPRS Negative", "BPRS Disorganized")
rownames(cor1_matrix) <- c("AX Error", "AY Error", "BX Error",
                           "BPRS Positive", "BPRS Negative", "BPRS Disorganized")

# create plot as a function
plot_topx_bprs <- function() {
  corrplot(
    cor1_matrix,
    method = "color",
    col = col_pal,
    is.corr = FALSE,
    col.lim = range(cor1_matrix, na.rm = TRUE),
    type = "lower",
    diag = TRUE,
    
    # create asterisks for significance - not using because overlaps with coeff
    # p.mat = p1_matrix,
    # sig.level = 0.05,
    # insig = "label_sig",
    # pch.cex = 0.8,
    insig = "blank",
    
    addCoef.col = "black",
    number.cex = 0.7,
    
    tl.col = "black",
    tl.pos = "t",
    tl.cex = 0.7,
    tl.srt = 45,
    
    cl.pos = "r",
    cl.cex = 0.7,
    cl.ratio = 0.2,
    cl.align.text = "l",
    
    title = "Correlations of TOPX and BPRS at Visit 1",
    cex.main = .9,
    mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1),
    frame.plot = TRUE
  )
}

# save plot
filename <- paste0("graphs/", format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d"), "_TOPX_BPRS.png")
png(filename, width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", res = 300)
plot_topx_bprs()
